- Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a directional trend (accelerating decay over the quarter) that slippage_trend can express. AC4 only measures the level of stale share at a threshold, not the acceleration of decay over time, so the substance of the trend claim is not covered. (consider check: slippage_trend)

Coverage guard: 2 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: AC4 uses slippage_trend with min_increase_pp=10, which measures increasing slippage but does not establish the causal link that decay drove the coverage decline. The claim asserts causation (decay → coverage drop), which no existing check can express as a causal relationship; slippage_trend measures the decay symptom but not that it was the driver of the coverage decline. The substance of the causal claim is not captured. (consider check: slippage_trend)

[note] Uncovered claim 'Once stale opportunities were removed, effective coverage was materially lower than reported' [PARAMETRIC]: AC6 uses stage_aging with max_stale_share_pct=40, which checks the share of stale opportunities, not the effective coverage after removal. The claim requires comparing effective coverage (post-removal) against reported coverage and showing it is materially lower. No existing check computes effective coverage net of stale opportunities; coverage_ratio only measures reported coverage. The substance (effective vs reported differential) is not expressible. (consider check: coverage_ratio)
Critic flagged 3 block issue(s) in the drafted criteria - one corrective re-draft.
Coverage guard: 2 gap(s); corrective re-draft...

- Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a directional increase in pipeline decay/staleness over the quarter. The existing slippage_trend check can express a trend in opportunity slippage, but no criterion in the drafted set measures a decay/staleness trend. AC4 only checks a stale-share level at a single point (and its max_stale_share_pct=60 threshold is a level check, not a trend), which cannot prove the decline was 'driven by accelerated' decay. (consider check: slippage_trend)

- Uncovered claim 'Once stale opportunities were removed, effective coverage was materially lower than reported' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim is a RELATIVE comparison: effective coverage (after removing stale opportunities) must be materially lower than the reported coverage. AC5 checks effective coverage against an absolute floor (min_multiple 2.5) but does not compare it against the reported coverage_ratio. No criterion measures the gap between reported and stale-adjusted coverage, so a dataset where adjusted coverage is not materially lower than reported would still pass. The direction (lower-than-reported) is the substance and is unmeasured. (consider check: coverage_ratio)
Drafted 8 criteria: AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8
Coverage guard: 2 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a causal mechanism (accelerated decay driving the coverage decline). AC5 uses slippage_trend with min_increase_pp=10, which measures revenue slippage, not pipeline decay/aging. The stage_aging check CAN express accelerated aging (opportunities exceeding the historical aging threshold), but AC4 only checks that stale share stays below 60% (a ceiling), not that aging accelerated over the quarter. No criterion measures the directional increase in aging that the claim requires. (consider check: stage_aging)

[note] Uncovered claim 'Once stale opportunities were removed, effective coverage was materially lower than reported' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim is relational: effective coverage (after removing stale) must be materially lower than reported coverage. AC6 checks coverage_ratio >= 2.5 at FY26-Q2, which only asserts an absolute floor. It does not compare effective coverage against reported coverage, so a dataset where effective coverage equals or exceeds reported coverage would pass AC6 while falsifying the claim. The coverage_ratio check can express this but the drafted parameters do not encode the reported-vs-effective comparison. (consider check: coverage_ratio)
